Erie, PA 34

Bayfront, Presque Isle, downtown, Millcreek

  1. Must see · Erie, PA

    Schaefer's Auto Art

    A free roadside sculpture garden of larger-than-life outsider art welded from old car and truck parts — a spider built from a whole VW Beetle, a bumblebee from a cement truck. One of northwest PA's most-photographed oddities; park in the gravel lot along Hershey Road.

    Look for ART

    3705 Hershey Rd, Erie, PA 16506

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Uncovering PA, PA Bucket List, Interestingpa

  2. Must see · Erie, PA

    Presque Isle State Park

    A 3,200-acre sandy peninsula arcing into Lake Erie — Pennsylvania's only 'seashore,' with 13 beaches, lagoons, a 13.5-mile multi-use trail and some of the best migratory birding in the state. Erie's single most-visited attraction and the geographic heart of the guide.

    Look for NATURE

    301 Peninsula Dr, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, VisitErie (Erie County CVB), Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  3. Must see · Erie, PA

    Erie Maritime Museum & U.S. Brig Niagara

    Bayfront museum and homeport of the U.S. Brig Niagara, a sailing reconstruction of Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry's relief flagship from the 1813 Battle of Lake Erie ('We have met the enemy and they are ours'). Exhibits on the battle and Great Lakes sail; the ship sails in season.

    Look for MARITIME

    150 E Front St, Erie, PA 16507

    Recommended by Erie Maritime Museum (official), National Maritime Historical Society, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  4. Must see · American & New American · Erie, PA

    New York Lunch (The Original)

    Opened 1927 and claims to be the first place to serve Erie's signature Greek dog; the Greek sauce is a spiced-up Greek pasta-sauce recipe brought by the city's early Greek restaurateurs, and it's the defining Erie street food.

    East Ave, Erie, PA 16504

    Recommended by Erie Reader (Erie alt-weekly), YourErie / Wjet-wfxp (Erie Abc/Fox affiliate), Nationalherald

  5. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Erie, PA

    Stanganelli's Italian Foods

    Making Erie's deep-fried pepperoni balls since 1961; so central to the city's identity that the Erie SeaWolves rebranded as the 'Pepperoni Balls' and QVC sold out 18,000 of Stanganelli's frozen ones in 2020.

    602 E 25th St, Erie, PA 16503

    Recommended by Erie Reader (Erie alt-weekly), YourErie / Wjet-wfxp (Erie Abc/Fox affiliate), Northwest Industrial Resource Center

  6. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · Erie, PA

    Lavery Brewing Co.

    A cornerstone of the Lake Erie Ale Trail — a downtown Erie brewery whose taproom is among the city's busiest, pouring a wide range of styles alongside a well-reviewed kitchen.

    128 W 12th St, Erie, PA 16501

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, VisitErie (Erie County CVB), Living the Dream (Lake Erie Ale Trail feature)

  7. Must see · American & New American · Erie, PA

    Lawrence Park Dinor

    A 1948 Silk City diner in Lawrence Park and the only 'dinor' — the northwest-PA spelling — on the National Register of Historic Places (2004). Seventy-five-plus years of counter-service classics, most famously the Greek omelet drowned in Erie's signature Greek sauce.

    4019 Main St, Erie, PA 16511

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Lake Erie Living

  8. Must see · Erie, PA

    Tom Ridge Environmental Center

    The free year-round gateway to Presque Isle — interactive exhibits on the peninsula's ecology, a big-screen orientation film and a glass-enclosed 75-foot observation tower over Lake Erie and Waldameer. Named for the Erie-raised former PA governor and Homeland Security secretary.

    Look for NATURE

    301 Peninsula Dr, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Uncovering PA

  9. Must see · Erie, PA

    Waldameer Park & Water World

    A family-owned amusement park at the doorstep of Presque Isle, open since 1896 and billed as the sixth-oldest continuously operating park in the U.S. Its wooden coaster Ravine Flyer II is a perennial Golden Ticket top-ten pick; free admission and parking, pay per ride.

    Look for AMUSEMENT

    220 Peninsula Dr, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by VisitErie (Erie County CVB), Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  10. Must see · Erie, PA

    Hagen History Center

    Erie County's history campus across four buildings, anchored by the 1891 Richardsonian-Romanesque Watson-Curtze Mansion (24 rooms, period interiors, exhibits on Erie's brewing and sporting heritage). Its grounds now also hold Frank Lloyd Wright's relocated original San Francisco office — a marquee addition making it one of northwest PA's top museums.

    Look for MUSEUM

    356 W 6th St, Erie, PA 16507

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, PA Route 6 Alliance

  11. Must see · American & New American · Erie, PA

    Sara's Restaurant

    The seasonal 1950s-themed drive-in guarding the entrance to Presque Isle since 1980 — vintage gas pumps, red picnic tables, char-grilled Smith's dogs and orange-vanilla twist; lines can run an hour at peak.

    25 Peninsula Dr, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by Interestingpa, Tour Erie PA / Erie Insider

  12. Must see · Sponge Candy & Sweets · Erie, PA

    Romolo Chocolates

    A four-generation Erie chocolatier whose sponge candy (and sponge-candy truffles) is a benchmark for the regional treat that can only be made in cool, dry weather; Erie sits in the heart of the 'Sponge Candy Crescent.'

    1525 W 8th St, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by NPR, Wandering Educators (travel writers' network)

  13. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · Erie, PA

    The Brewerie at Union Station

    A brewpub set in Erie's historic Union Station — trains still stop upstairs — pairing fresh house ales with a scratch menu; consistently rated among the best restaurants in the city.

    123 W 14th St, Erie, PA 16501

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, VisitErie (Erie County CVB)

  14. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Perry Monument

    An 80-foot limestone obelisk on Crystal Point at Presque Isle, dedicated 1926 on the 113th anniversary of the Battle of Lake Erie, honoring Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry and the sailors who built and sailed his fleet from Erie's harbor in 1813. Sited to be visible from the mainland across Misery Bay.

    Look for MONUMENT

    Crystal Point, Presque Isle State Park, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), The Historical Marker Database

  15. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Erie Bluffs State Park

    A 587-acre undeveloped stretch of Lake Erie shoreline twelve miles west of the city, where trails run through oak savanna and along 90-foot bluffs to a wild, uncrowded beach and the mouth of Elk Creek — the quiet, rugged counterpart to Presque Isle.

    Look for NATURE

    11122 West Lake Rd, Girard, PA 16417

    Recommended by PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Uncovering PA, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  16. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Splash Lagoon Indoor Water Park Resort

    A Polynesian-themed indoor water park kept at 84 degrees year-round — nine slides, a 30,000-square-foot wave pool, a FlowRider and a five-story treehouse — attached to several hotels off Peach Street. One of Erie's top family attractions, rain or snow.

    Look for AMUSEMENT

    8091 Peach St, Erie, PA 16509

    Recommended by VisitPA (Pennsylvania Tourism Office), Uncovering PA, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  17. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Asbury Woods

    A free 234-acre Millcreek nature preserve with five miles of trails, a boardwalk through a wooded wetland and a year-round nature center — a beloved local spot for birding, maple-sugaring programs and easy family walks.

    Look for NATURE

    4105 Asbury Rd, Erie, PA 16506

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, PA Bucket List, ExplorePAHistory (witf)

  18. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    North Pier Lighthouse

    The shortest of Erie's three lighthouses at 34 feet, standing at the tip of Presque Isle where the bay meets the lake — and the last square, pyramidal-style light tower left in the United States. A 20-minute drive from the park entrance and a favorite sunset perch.

    Look for LANDMARK

    North Pier, Presque Isle State Park, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, PA Bucket List, VisitPA (Pennsylvania Tourism Office)

  19. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Bicentennial Tower

    A 187-foot observation tower at Dobbins Landing on the bayfront, built in 1995–96 for Erie's bicentennial, with two decks giving panoramic views of Presque Isle Bay, the peninsula and downtown.

    Look for VIEW

    1 State St, Erie, PA 16507

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Erie Times-News / GoErie

  20. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Erie Art Museum

    Downtown museum (rooted in the 1898 Art Club of Erie) holding 8,000-plus objects with notable strengths in American ceramics, Tibetan paintings, Indian bronzes, photography and comic art — the leading visual-arts institution in northwest PA.

    Look for MUSEUM

    20 E 5th St, Erie, PA 16501

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), VisitErie (Erie County CVB)

  21. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Warner Theatre

    A 1931 Art Deco / French Renaissance movie palace by Rapp & Rapp, saved by the city and reborn as a performing-arts center — home to the Erie Philharmonic and Lake Erie Ballet and a linchpin of the downtown revival.

    Look for ARCH

    811 State St, Erie, PA 16501

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), ExplorePAHistory (witf)

  22. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Presque Isle Lighthouse

    An 1872 lighthouse on the sandy north shore of Presque Isle, still an active aid to navigation; in season visitors tour the keeper's house and climb 78 steps to the lantern for a sweeping Lake Erie view.

    Look for LANDMARK

    301 Peninsula Dr (Presque Isle), Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, Presque Isle Lighthouse (official)

  23. Worth the detour · Erie, PA

    Dobbins Landing

    The public wharf at the foot of State Street where the city meets Presque Isle Bay — the waterfront hub holding the Bicentennial Tower, boat-tour and fishing-charter docks and the seasonal water taxi across to Presque Isle. Named for Daniel Dobbins, the Erie sailing master who helped build Perry's fleet.

    Look for LANDMARK

    1 State St, Erie, PA 16507

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Uncovering PA

  24. Worth the detour · Sponge Candy & Sweets · Erie, PA

    Pulakos Chocolates

    Erie chocolatier tracing to Greek immigrant George Pulakos in 1889; known for sponge taffy, French truffles and a 25-minute factory tour with samples — the old-guard counterpart to Romolo in Erie's chocolate scene.

    2530 Parade St, Erie, PA 16503

    Recommended by PBS, Wandering Educators (travel writers' network)

  25. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · Erie, PA

    Erie Brewing Company

    Founded as a brewpub in 1993 and a full brewery since 1999, Erie Brewing has taken three Great American Beer Festival medals and distributes across more than a dozen states — the veteran of the local scene.

    Erie, PA 16501

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Uncovering PA

  26. Worth the detour · Italian & Pizza · Erie, PA

    Colao's Ristorante

    Family-owned since 1999, cooking authentic Italian from recipes passed down for generations — a locals' pick for Erie's Italian dining rooted in the city's deep Italian community.

    2826 Plum St, Erie, PA 16508

    Recommended by VisitErie (Erie County CVB), Keystone

  27. Worth the detour · BBQ & Smokehouse · Erie, PA

    Federal Hill Smokehouse

    Bringing slow-smoked Texas barbecue to far-northern PA near Erie's Little Italy at 26th and Peach; a frequently top-cited Erie meat destination.

    W 26th St & Peach St, Erie, PA 16508

    Recommended by VisitErie (Erie County CVB), Keystone

  28. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · Erie, PA

    Black Monk Brewery

    A small west-side brewery on the Lake Erie Ale Trail devoted to Belgian styles (dubbels, tripels, quads) with 16-plus taps and rotating food trucks — a distinctive specialist among Erie's breweries.

    3721 W 12th St, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, Brewerspa

  29. Deep cut · Erie, PA

    Wayne Blockhouse

    An 1880 state-built replica of the Fort Presque Isle blockhouse marking where General 'Mad' Anthony Wayne died in 1796 — and the site of one of early America's strangest burials: his flesh was boiled from his bones in 1809 so the skeleton could be carried to eastern PA, and the boiled remains reburied here.

    Look for HIST

    Soldiers & Sailors Home grounds, 560 E 3rd St, Erie, PA 16507

    Recommended by The Historical Marker Database, Roadside America, Hagenhistory

  30. Deep cut · Erie, PA

    Erie Land Lighthouse

    One of the first two lighthouses on the Great Lakes (first tower 1818), the present stone tower crowns a bluff east of downtown — the second of Erie's three historic lights (with Presque Isle and the North Pier Light).

    Look for LANDMARK

    2 Lighthouse St, Erie, PA 16507

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, PA Route 6 Alliance

  31. Deep cut · Erie, PA

    Erie Zoo

    A compact, well-regarded zoo along Mill Creek with some 400 animals and a kiddieland train — a longtime family staple in the city's south side.

    Look for ZOO

    423 W 38th St, Erie, PA 16508

    Recommended by VisitErie (Erie County CVB), Uncovering PA

  32. Deep cut · Erie, PA

    Erie Playhouse

    One of the oldest and largest community theaters in the country (founded 1916), staging a full season of musicals and plays downtown — a cornerstone of Erie's grassroots arts life.

    Look for ARCH

    13 W 10th St, Erie, PA 16501

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), VisitErie (Erie County CVB)

  33. Deep cut · Erie, PA

    Erie Cemetery

    A 75-acre garden cemetery laid out in 1851 between Chestnut and Cherry, a leafy walk of Victorian monuments and a Civil War veterans' section. Among its famous residents are composer Harry T. Burleigh and many of the industrialists who built Erie — the city's outdoor history book.

    Look for CEMETERY

    2116 Chestnut St, Erie, PA 16502

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Erie Cemetery Association (official)

  34. Deep cut · Erie, PA

    Frontier Park

    A shaded west-side greenspace along Cascade Creek with an outdoor amphitheater — home each summer to free Frontier Friday concerts and, on the first weekend of August, the 30-plus-year-old Erie Blues & Jazz Festival that draws thousands.

    Look for PARK

    1501 W 6th St, Erie, PA 16505

    Recommended by Erie Reader (Erie alt-weekly), Erie News Now — Wicu/Wsee

North East & the Lake Erie wine belt 3

  1. Worth the detour · North East & the Lake Erie wine belt

    Lake Erie Wine Country (Concord Grape Belt)

    The 20-plus-winery belt straddling Erie County, PA and Chautauqua County, NY — one of the world's largest concentrations of Concord vineyards and the heart of Welch's grape production, best toured as a scenic drive of tasting rooms around North East.

    Look for SCENIC

    North East, PA 16428

    Recommended by PA Eats (Pennsylvania food/drink editorial), Travel Addicts (travel blog, real track record)

  2. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · North East & the Lake Erie wine belt

    Penn Shore Winery

    One of the first two wineries in Pennsylvania to get a limited-winery license after Prohibition (1968), crushing its first grapes in 1969 — a foundational stop on the Lake Erie Wine Country trail.

    10225 East Lake Rd, North East, PA 16428

    Recommended by PA Eats (Pennsylvania food/drink editorial), Interestingpa

  3. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · North East & the Lake Erie wine belt

    Arrowhead Wine Cellars

    Nick and Kathy Mobilia's farm winery since 1998, making wine from grapes and fruit grown on their own 250 acres — European varietals (Pinot Grigio, Riesling) alongside native Niagara, Catawba and Concord.

    12073 East Main Rd, North East, PA 16428

    Recommended by Travel Addicts (travel blog, real track record), Interestingpa

Meadville & Crawford County 4

Allegheny College, Market House

  1. Must see · Meadville & Crawford County

    Meadville Market House

    Built in 1870 and community-rescued in 1970, the oldest continuously operating public market structure in Pennsylvania — 50-plus vendors selling produce, meats, baked goods and crafts, and the civic heart of this Allegheny College town.

    Look for MARKET

    910 Market St, Meadville, PA 16335

    Recommended by Interestingpa, Visit Crawford County PA, The Historical Marker Database

  2. Must see · Meadville & Crawford County

    Pymatuning Spillway (Where the Ducks Walk on the Fish)

    The Linesville spillway on Pennsylvania's largest lake, where carp mass so thickly below the dam that ducks and geese appear to walk across their backs to reach the fish pellets tourists toss in — a genuine Pennsylvania roadside phenomenon drawing 300,000-plus visitors a year and Linesville's town motto.

    Look for ODDITY

    12318 Hartstown Rd, Linesville, PA 16424

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, Visit Crawford County PA, Roadside America

  3. Worth the detour · Meadville & Crawford County

    Baldwin-Reynolds House Museum

    The 1843 Greek Revival mansion begun as the dream home of U.S. Supreme Court Justice Henry Baldwin, later home to businessman William Reynolds and now the house museum of the Crawford County Historical Society, filled with Baldwin and Reynolds furnishings; as of 2025 open year-round for the first time in its 60-plus-year history.

    Look for MUSEUM

    639 Terrace St, Meadville, PA 16335

    Recommended by Uncovering PA, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Visit Crawford County PA

  4. Worth the detour · Meadville & Crawford County

    Allegheny College

    Founded in 1815, the oldest college west of the Allegheny Mountains — a leafy liberal-arts campus (Bentley Hall, Bousson) that gives Meadville its college-town energy and cultural programming.

    Look for HIST

    520 N Main St, Meadville, PA 16335

    Recommended by Allegheny College (official), Visit Crawford County PA

Edinboro & Cambridge Springs 4

  1. Must see · Edinboro & Cambridge Springs

    Goodell Gardens & Homestead

    An 80-acre botanical garden and accredited arboretum on the former Goodell family farm, with formal gardens, 60-plus tree species (including a Franklin tree and dawn redwood), rhododendron and pollinator displays and a concert/event series; students get in free.

    Look for GARDEN

    221 Waterford St, Edinboro, PA 16412

    Recommended by VisitPA (Pennsylvania Tourism Office), ArbNet / Morton Register of Arboreta, PA Route 6 Alliance

  2. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · Edinboro & Cambridge Springs

    Riverside Brewing Co.

    Opened 2019 in a refurbished 19th-century barn along French Creek on the grounds of the lost Riverside Inn, this farm-to-table brewpub is an outgrowth of the four-generation Howles Maple Farm and folds its own maple into beer and food; live music and outdoor summer series.

    1 Fountain Ave, Cambridge Springs, PA 16403

    Recommended by Visit Crawford County PA, VisitPA (Pennsylvania Tourism Office)

  3. Worth the detour · Edinboro & Cambridge Springs

    Edinboro Lake

    A 245-acre glacial lake at the center of this college town, rated unlimited-horsepower for water-skiing, with the guarded Pat Crawford Beach, public boat launches and kayak/canoe/pontoon rentals at Edinboro Lake Resort — the town's warm-weather focal point.

    Look for NATURE

    Edinboro, PA 16412

    Recommended by VisitErie (Erie County CVB), VisitPA (Pennsylvania Tourism Office)

  4. Worth the detour · Sponge Candy & Sweets · Edinboro & Cambridge Springs

    Edinboro Chocolaterie

    A downtown Edinboro chocolatier opened in 2019 by the family behind Butler's long-running Peter's Chocolate Shoppe; small-batch fillings made on site, hand-dipped nuts and clusters, and chocolate-covered raspberries, strawberries and Granny Smith apples.

    114 Erie St, Edinboro, PA 16412

    Recommended by Erie News Now — Wicu/Wsee, Eced

Grove City, Mercer & Slippery Rock 6

  1. Must see · Grove City, Mercer & Slippery Rock

    Wendell August Forge

    America's oldest and largest working forge (since 1932), part artisan workshop and part gallery — watch smiths hand-hammer aluminum, bronze and pewter giftware, trays and ornaments on the factory floor.

    Look for CRAFT

    620 Madison Ave, Grove City, PA 16127

    Recommended by Visit Mercer County PA, Wendell August Forge (official)

  2. Worth the detour · Grove City, Mercer & Slippery Rock

    Old Stone House

    An 1822 stagecoach inn and tavern built by John Brown on the old Pittsburgh-to-Erie Pike, later a post office and Civil War muster point; reconstructed in 1963 and now a free museum of rural life owned and run by Slippery Rock University, open weekends May through October.

    Look for HIST

    PA-8 at PA-173, Slippery Rock, PA 16057

    Recommended by Slippery Rock University (official), Experience Butler County PA (CVB), The Clio

  3. Worth the detour · Grove City, Mercer & Slippery Rock

    Wolf Creek Narrows Natural Area

    A 243-acre Western Pennsylvania Conservancy preserve near Slippery Rock where Wolf Creek cuts a gorge with 50-foot rock walls; a 1.5-mile loop trail runs through one of the state's most diverse spring wildflower displays — Virginia bluebells, trillium, trout-lily — peaking mid-April to May.

    Look for NATURE

    Mountville Rd, Slippery Rock, PA 16057

    Recommended by Western Pennsylvania Conservancy, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, Uncovering PA

  4. Worth the detour · Grove City, Mercer & Slippery Rock

    Grove City Premium Outlets

    One of Pennsylvania's biggest outlet destinations — 100-plus open-air brand stores (Coach, Michael Kors, The North Face, Columbia) with tax-free clothing, right off I-79 exit 113.

    Look for SHOPPING

    1911 Leesburg Grove City Rd, Grove City, PA 16127

    Recommended by Visit Mercer County PA, Simon / Grove City Premium Outlets (official)

  5. Worth the detour · Grove City, Mercer & Slippery Rock

    Grove City College

    A handsome Gothic-collegiate campus (founded 1876) known for its independence from federal funding; the Harbison Chapel and the college's grounds are the centerpiece of this Mercer County town.

    Look for CAMPUS

    100 Campus Dr, Grove City, PA 16127

    Recommended by Visit Mercer County PA, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  6. Worth the detour · Grove City, Mercer & Slippery Rock

    Living Treasures Animal Park (Moraine)

    An interactive walk-through wild-animal park four miles from the Moraine/I-79 exit where visitors hand-feed deer, hold reptiles and get face-to-face with 300-plus animals across dozens of species — a family stop near Moraine and McConnells Mill.

    Look for FAMILY

    268 Fox Rd, New Castle, PA 16101

    Recommended by VisitPA (Pennsylvania Tourism Office), Visit Mercer County PA

I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh 8

Conneaut Lake, Zelienople, Harmony, Cranberry

  1. Must see · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    Harmony Historic District

    A National Historic Landmark district (designated 1974) preserving the old-world German village founded in 1804 by the Harmony Society — 50-plus early buildings, the Harmony Museum and a Harmonist cemetery, half an hour north of Pittsburgh near Zelienople.

    Look for HIST

    Main St, Harmony, PA 16037

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Experience Butler County PA (CVB), Pittsburgh Magazine

  2. Must see · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    Conneaut Lake Park

    A trolley-era lakeside amusement park dating to 1892 on Pennsylvania's largest natural lake, home to the 1938 Blue Streak wooden coaster and the world's oldest Tumble Bug ride. Beloved and much-imperiled — its operating season has run hot and cold under successive owners, so check ahead.

    Look for AMUSEMENT

    12382 Center St, Conneaut Lake, PA 16316

    Recommended by Visit Crawford County PA, Interestingpa

  3. Must see · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    McConnells Mill State Park

    2,546 acres of the Slippery Rock Creek Gorge — a National Natural Landmark of whitewater, boulders and hemlock — with a restored 1800s gristmill and a covered bridge; hiking, climbing and kayaking about 40 miles north of Pittsburgh off I-79.

    Look for NATURE

    McConnells Mill Rd, Portersville, PA 16051

    Recommended by PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  4. Worth the detour · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    Moraine State Park

    A reclaimed strip-mine and oil-field turned 3,225-acre Lake Arthur, with two swimming beaches, sailing, and a paved lakeside bike trail — two miles from McConnells Mill along the I-79 corridor.

    Look for NATURE

    225 Pleasant Valley Rd, Portersville, PA 16051

    Recommended by PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts)

  5. Worth the detour · American & New American · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    Harmony Inn

    A historic tavern in the heart of Harmony's National Historic Landmark district, now run by North Country Brewing, serving German-inflected comfort food in a storied (and reputedly haunted) old building.

    230 Mercer St, Harmony, PA 16037

    Recommended by Experience Butler County PA (CVB), Pittsburgh Magazine

  6. Deep cut · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    Passavant House

    The first house built in Zelienople (1808-1810), home of Philippe Passavant and Zelie Basse, daughter of the town's founder; now the Zelienople Historical Society's house museum with early-1800s Passavant-family furnishings and a period herb garden, tours by appointment.

    Look for HIST

    243 S Main St, Zelienople, PA 16063

    Recommended by Experience Butler County PA (CVB), ExplorePAHistory (witf), Butler Eagle

  7. Deep cut · Breweries, Wineries & Beer · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    Conneaut Cellars Winery & Distillery

    A lakeside winery and distillery beside Conneaut Lake that hosts summer live-music and outdoor tasting series — the drinks anchor of the Conneaut Lake resort area on the corridor.

    Conneaut Lake, PA 16316

    Recommended by Visit Crawford County PA, Interestingpa

  8. Closed — kept for the record · I-79 corridor south to Pittsburgh

    Riverside Inn — CLOSED

    The grand 1885 mineral-springs resort and dinner theater that made Cambridge Springs a Gilded-Age destination (NRHP 1978) was destroyed by fire on May 2, 2017. Kept flagged: the site now hosts the Riverside Brewing Company, but the historic inn itself is gone.

    Look for HIST

    1 Fountain Ave, Cambridge Springs, PA 16403

    Recommended by Wikipedia (sights / institutional facts), Erie News Now — Wicu/Wsee, Meadville Tribune

41 sights and 18 places to eat across Erie, PA — the Bayfront and Presque Isle — the Lake Erie wine belt at North East, and the I-79/US-19 corridor south toward Pittsburgh through Meadville, Edinboro and Grove City. Each is traceable to the source that named it. Erie’s canon is its own: the Greek-sauce hot dog, Stanganelli’s pepperoni balls, sponge candy, Great-Lakes perch, and the wineries & breweries — plus Presque Isle, the U.S. Brig Niagara and the Bicentennial Tower.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Erie’s canon is its own: the Greek-sauce hot dog (New York Lunch, Sara’s), deep-fried pepperoni balls (Stanganelli’s), sponge candy (Romolo, Pulakos), Federal Hill Italian, Great-Lakes perch & walleye fish fries, and the Lake Erie wine belt (Mazza, Penn Shore, Arrowhead), sourced to the Erie Times-News and Erie Reader. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — the Erie Times-News/GoErie, Erie Reader, Visit Erie, the Meadville Tribune, PA DCNR, NPS, Uncovering PA, Atlas Obscura and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
